summary: Yutang Lin was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at St. John's University (~1912–1916), Harvard University (~1919–1920), and the University of Leipzig under August Conrady (~1921–1923). He held a post at Peking University (~1923–1926).

Yuto Kawamura is an Indology scholar who was a postdoc fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Yuzo Mizoguchi (1932–2010) worked in Sinology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Saitama University, Hitotsubashi University, and Daito Bunka University.

Yönten Gyatso (1932–2002) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (~1947–1959) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he served as a Tibetan Studies research advisor (~1970–1997).
Yūki Takamu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Takamu studied at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and held a post there as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) in 2017.
Zack Beer is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (both attested 2026).

Zaifu Liu is a Sinologist who studied at Xiamen University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, University of Chicago, Stockholm University, University of Colorado Boulder, City University of Hong Kong, and HKUST.

Zarawar Khan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1931) under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1931) and later studied at the University of Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and held a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).
Zellig S. Harris (1909–1992) was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University.

Zeng Yang works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen.
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji from around 1932 to 1936.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of California (~1943–1947), with traditional teachers including Richard Baker and Sojun Mel Weitsman, and served as co-abbess at San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Hanazono University (~1939–1974) and Otani University.
Zenno Ikuno (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University, later serving as professor and emeritus professor there, and held posts at Shukutoku Junior College, Shukutoku University, and the Sanko Research Institute.

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899) and held posts at the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Kyoto universities. He held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute, and Kyoto National Museum.

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1976) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Rissho University, and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
